questions.question: Why did WTG-07 repeatedly trip on gearbox oil over-temperature in 2026, and what was done about it?

answer.text:
WTG-07 repeatedly tripped because its gearbox oil cooler could not reject enough heat at high load: the cooler fan was running slowly, the radiator fins were about 40% blocked by insects and pollen, and the fan motor bearing on LWS-P-30418 had failed with motor current 35% above nominal.[1][2][3] The 8D’s root cause was a preventive-maintenance gap: radiator cleaning and fan checks were not scheduled at a fixed interval, which allowed fan-bearing failure and radiator fouling to reduce cooling capacity.[4][5] The symptom pattern was WTG-07-specific: from 2026-04-09 to 2026-06-21 it logged 27 A2101 high-temperature warnings and two A2102 trips, while no other turbine logged an A2101 warning in the same period.[6]

The immediate containment was to limit WTG-07 to 2.6 MW from 2026-06-01 and check oil temperature daily; that limit was removed on 2026-06-25 after corrective actions.[7] The corrective actions were to replace the oil cooler fan motor LWS-P-30418 on WO-26-0398, clean the oil cooler radiator on WO-26-0399, remove the 2.6 MW limit after verification, and keep a separate HSS bearing replacement WO-26-0412 open pending bearing delivery.[8] For prevention, task MP-GBX-07, “Oil cooler radiator cleaning and fan current check,” was added to the maintenance plan for all turbines every 6 months in issue 2 of 2026-07-01.[9] Verification as of the 8D report was that WTG-07 had no A2101 warning since 2026-06-24, but the vibration issue would remain above alarm level until the bearing replacement, and the 8D would close only after WO-26-0412 plus an oil sample 500 operating hours after bearing replacement.[10][11]

questions.question: Why do WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 stop at night in summer?

answer.text:
WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 stop at night in summer because they are under a bat-protection curtailment condition: from 1 June to 31 August, they must stop between 22:00 and 05:00 local time when hub-height wind speed is below 6.0 m/s and air temperature is 10 °C or higher.[1]  

The stated reason is protection of a protected bat species: Skelvane Wood, east of WTG-03 to WTG-05, has a maternity roost, and the bats forage near those turbines on warm, calm summer nights.[1]  

This is an automatic turbine-control setting rather than an operator fault; the permit says the curtailment is implemented automatically and recorded in the turbine event log, and the June O&M minutes say the 2026 season started on 1 June with the controller settings checked on 2026-05-28.[1][2]  

The shift handovers also describe the stops as normal “bat curtailment” during low wind and say not to reset them.[3][4]  

SCADA records match that explanation: on 2026-06-01 and 2026-08-25, WTG-03/04/05 entered status S420 “Curtailed - environmental condition” at about 22:00 with low wind and warm temperatures, then ended around 05:00.[5]

questions.question: What does CCV mean, and which Quellmoor Ridge turbines does service bulletin SB-LWS-2025-07 apply to?

answer.text:
CCV means “Cold Climate Version,” an LT-32 variant with gearbox oil heaters, low-temperature steel and heated sensors [1].

questions.question: Which gear oil does the LT-32 maintenance manual specify, and does SOP-GBX-010 Rev. B agree?

answer.text:
The LT-32 maintenance manual specifies **Proseware PWG 320 gear oil, ISO VG 320, synthetic PAO**, with a total oil volume of **410 L** [1].  

**No, SOP-GBX-010 Rev. B does not agree with that manual value**: it calls for **Proseware PWG 220 (ISO VG 220)**, **470 L per turbine** made up of **60 L flush + 410 L fill** [2]. The SOP’s PWG 220 requirement aligns with SB-LWS-2025-07 Rev. A, which amends LWS-MM-GBX-32 Rev. D for applicable LT-32 CCV turbines and instructs draining PWG 320, flushing with 60 L of PWG 220, and filling with 410 L of PWG 220 [3].

questions.question: Use the troubleshoot-alarm skill: WTG-07 raises alarm A2101 again. What does the alarm mean, what caused it before and what should the technician check?

answer.text:
A2101 means **“Gearbox oil sump temperature high (75 °C)”**; for WTG-07, treat a repeat as a gearbox cooling/oil/bearing fault until proven otherwise, and do not wait for an A2102 trip at 82 °C before inspecting the cooling circuit and condition indicators [1].

Previously, WTG-07 had **27 A2101 warnings** between 2026-04-09 and 2026-06-21, plus **two A2102 trips** at 82.6 °C and 83.4 °C; the 8D says no other turbine logged A2101 in that same period [2].  
The prior root cause was inadequate oil-cooler heat rejection at high load [3].  
The immediate physical causes found before were reduced cooler-fan speed, radiator fins about **40 % blocked by insects and pollen**, and a failed fan-motor bearing with motor current **35 % above nominal** [4][5].  
After the June repair, verification said there had been no A2101 on WTG-07 since 2026-06-24, but vibration remained above alarm level until the HSS bearing was replaced [6].

Technician checks, in order:  
1. Check oil-cooler fan rotation and motor current, because the OEM A2101 table lists cooler fan fault/reduced speed as a possible cause and the previous WTG-07 case found elevated motor current from a failed fan-motor bearing [1][5].  
2. Inspect and clean the oil-cooler radiator fins, because the OEM check is “clean the radiator” and the earlier blockage was about 40 % from insects and pollen [1][4].  
3. Check the thermostatic valve insert **LWS-P-30422**, because the OEM A2101 checks include that valve insert [1].  
4. Check gearbox oil level, because low oil level is an OEM-listed A2101 cause and “check the oil level” is an OEM action [1].  
5. Review the vibration trend and take an oil sample, because the OEM lists bearing damage as a possible A2101 cause and specifies both checks [1].  
6. Specifically check the open HSS-bearing issue before returning WTG-07 to normal operation, because later correspondence says WO-26-0412 for WTG-07 HSS bearing replacement could not start until bearings arrived and that WTG-07 was running with vibration above alarm level with weekly vibration reviews requested [7].  
7. If parts status matters for dispatch, note that the same correspondence said the last HSS bearing had been used on WTG-10 and that two bearings were confirmed for delivery in week 39, 21–25 September 2026 [8].

questions.question: Use the audit-readiness skill to prepare the regulator's review of the bat protection curtailment: which permit conditions apply and what evidence exists?

answer.text:
Direct answer: the bat-curtailment review should focus on EP-2018-0417 conditions 7.1–7.6, plus the annual-report due date in condition 10.1 and the site-copy requirement in condition 1.3.[1][2]

| Requirement | Evidence found | Status | Gap or action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Keep the current permit at site: condition 1.3 says “A copy of this permit shall be kept at the site.”[1] | Current consolidated permit EP-2018-0417 incorporates variation 2 dated 2024-12-10 for “bat protection curtailment (condition 7.3).”[1] | Ready for review if the site copy can be produced.[1] | Bring the site copy of the consolidated permit to the regulator meeting.[1] |
| Monitor bat activity at WTG-04 nacelle with an acoustic detector from April to October each year under condition 7.1.[2] | The wiki search found the permit requirement, but no separate acoustic-detector dataset or monitoring-result document was found. | Gap. | Locate the WTG-04 nacelle acoustic-detector records for April–October and include them in the review pack.[2] |
| Report the monitoring results in the annual environmental report under condition 7.2.[2] | The permit also requires annual environmental report submission by 31 January under condition 10.1.[2] | Gap for evidence currently in the wiki. | Provide the annual environmental report, or if the 2026 report is not yet due, show the draft/reporting plan and due date control.[2] |
| Stop WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 from 1 June to 31 August, 22:00–05:00 local time, when hub-height wind speed is below 6.0 m/s and air temperature is 10 °C or higher under condition 7.3.[2] | The site layout labels “WTG-03 to WTG-05” as the environmental permit curtailment group, and also labels Skelvane Wood as the bat roost.[3][4] | Ready for review on scope/location.[2][3][4] | Use the layout as supporting context, noting it is OCR-derived evidence.[3][4] |
| Implement bat curtailment automatically by the turbine control system under condition 7.4.[2] | The 2026-06-18 O&M minutes say the bat protection curtailment season started on 1 June for WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05, and that Yusuf Arkwell checked the curtailment settings in the turbine controllers on 2026-05-28.[5] | Partly ready. | Keep controller-setting screenshots/configuration export with the minutes, because the minutes evidence the check but not the controller values themselves.[5] |
| Record each curtailment period in the turbine event log under condition 7.4.[2] | The SCADA table contains S420 “Curtailed - environmental condition” records for WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05, with 32 START and 32 END events per turbine; first STARTs are 2026-06-01 22:00:04/07/10 and last ENDs are 2026-08-30 05:00:06/09/12.[6] | Ready for sampled event-log evidence across the 2026 season covered by the SCADA export.[6] | For the review pack, export the full filtered S420 event list rather than only samples or aggregates.[6] |
| Keep curtailment records for 5 years and summarise them in the annual report under condition 7.5.[2] | The available SCADA export provides deterministic-table evidence of 2026 S420 events through the latest queried row range.[6] | Partial. | Retention cannot be proven from one 2026 export alone; show document-control/retention location and prior-year curtailment archives.[2][6] |
| Allow for possible threshold adjustment after three years of monitoring data under condition 7.6.[2] | No Authority threshold-adjustment record was found in the reviewed bat-curtailment sources. | No current change evidenced. | Ask the regulator whether condition 7.6 has been exercised and keep any Authority correspondence with the permit file.[2] |
| Operational awareness: do not reset normal bat curtailment stops.[7] | The 2026-07-15 shift handover told operators that WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 would stop from 22:00 if wind stayed low due to bat curtailment and that this was normal and should not be reset.[7] | Ready as operator-awareness evidence. | Include handover note in pack as supporting evidence, not as a substitute for event-log records.[7] |
| Operational awareness during low-wind nights continued later in the season.[8] | The 2026-07-29 shift handover states: “Night: WTG-03, WTG-04 and WTG-05 bat curtailment expected again (low wind).”[8] | Ready as supporting evidence. | Include with SCADA evidence to show the control was understood during operations.[8] |

Summary: requirements 7.3 and 7.4 have direct evidence from the permit, controller-setting check minutes, and SCADA S420 event records.[2][5][6] Requirements 7.1, 7.2, 7.5 and 10.1 need additional pack evidence: acoustic monitoring data, the annual environmental report or reporting plan, and retention/archive proof.[2] The spatial basis for the curtailment group and bat roost is supported by the site layout, but that evidence is OCR and should be treated as supporting context rather than the primary permit requirement.[3][4]
